problem:
Which of the following are orthogonal projection matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{13} & \frac{6}{13} \\ -\frac{6}{13} & \frac{4}{13}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{26} & \frac{5}{26} \\ \frac{5}{26} & \frac{25}{26}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4} & \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Recall that $Q$ is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if ${Q}^{2}=Q$ and ${Q}^{T}=Q.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\ne A.\end{aligned}
$$

- $B$ is an orthogonal projection matrix. We have
${B}^{T}=B$
and 

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{26} & \frac{5}{26} \\ \frac{5}{26} & \frac{25}{26}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{26} & \frac{5}{26} \\ \frac{5}{26} & \frac{25}{26}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 25\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 25\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{676}[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 25\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 25\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{676}[\begin{aligned}26 & 130 \\ 130 & 650\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{26} & \frac{5}{26} \\ \frac{5}{26} & \frac{25}{26}\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

- $C$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{T}\ne C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only."
